# Krate

Krate lets developers package software as one .krate file that runs through native Krate runtimes on macOS, Windows and Linux.

The recipient installs a compatible Krate runtime once. Applications use supported Krate APIs; existing desktop binaries do not become portable without adaptation.

The Krate runtime is free and open source (MIT OR Apache-2.0). Studio has separate licensing; see the repository license details. Krate Studio provides AI-assisted app creation and revision. Developers can also build against the Rust SDK. Optional hosted services are separate from the local runtime and file format.

A .krate bundle contains a WebAssembly component and manifest, and can also carry source, SDK interfaces and assets. Full bundle bytes, uncompressed code payload, runtime download and installed runtime size are different measurements.

Applications begin without file or network access and receive approved capabilities through the runtime. This boundary is not a guarantee of bug-free or harmless software; review the threat model and only run apps you trust.

## Current measurements

From the Krate Benchmark Register, compiled 2026-09-26 for runtime and CLI 0.5.1 (commit 774ec7f35). Each figure is shown with the status the Register gives it.

- Same file on three systems [Current; Register §9]: Ten ported apps, the same bundle bytes on each system, ran on macOS, Ubuntu and Windows GitHub CI runners with runtime 0.5.1: 10 of 10 pass on all three. One app has no replay check. CI run: https://github.com/incyashraj/krate/actions/runs/35552275372
- App size [Current; Register §1.1]: The compiled app component (code.wasm) of ten shipped apps is 18 to 31 KB, for example krate-clock 18,042 B, board 28,210 B and streak 30,512 B (packed 2026-08-26).
- Full shareable bundle [Current; Register §1.1]: The full .krate bundle also carries the app's source and SDK so a shared app can be edited. Examples: clock 100,744 B, board 108,974 B, streak 110,742 B.
- First-time download [Current (E6); Register §1.2, E6]: A first-time recipient downloads the Krate Player zip plus the 37,489-byte benchmark notes app: 11,553,801 B, against 111,418,578 B for the MarkText 0.17.1 zip. That is 9.64x smaller. A returning recipient downloads only the app, 37,489 B. MarkText does far more; this compares packaging, not features.
- First-time install [Current (E6); Register §1.2, E6]: Installed, Krate Player v0.3.0 plus the app take 25,592 KiB, against 291,468 KiB for MarkText 0.17.1 ARM64: 11.39x smaller.
- Memory [Current; Register §3.1, E6.1]: Notes app against MarkText 0.17.1 on an Apple M4 MacBook Air, runtime 0.5.1, window on a 1x display, settled after 30 s, n=10: Krate 73.5 MiB at 5,000 lines and 95.7 MiB at 50,000 lines; MarkText 358.5 MiB and 2,093.9 MiB. With Krate's window on a 2x display, Krate measured 147.9 and 175.0 MiB (n=8 to 10). Memory is macOS footprint, not RSS.
- Speed against native code [Current, n=9; Register §2.2]: Krate is not faster than native code. A Krate hex viewer ran 2.7x to 21.0x slower than native hexyl across 8 workloads. The gap is widest on tiny inputs, where a fixed cost of about 90 to 100 ms to start and set up dominates, and shrinks as the work grows.
- Energy [Not measured; Register §4]: Energy and battery use have not been measured, so no energy or battery claim is made.

## Historical (2026-08-25)

The following is the recorded 2026-08-25 notes comparison, not a measurement of the latest release or all Krate apps.
MarkText 0.17.1 ARM64 vs the Krate notes replica, Apple M4, macOS 27 (build 26A5388g), on AC power; equivalent-workload comparison, not feature parity.

- Historical app bundle versus installed application: Krate 36.6 KiB; MarkText 284.6 MiB installed.
- memory, 50,000-line document: Krate 178.5 MiB, one process; MarkText 2,299.4 MiB across four processes.
- warm start to a visible window, 50,000-line document: Krate 237.1 ms median; MarkText 611.5 ms median.

The historical Krate runtime was installed separately at 88.6 MiB. The 36.6 KiB app bundle is not the total first-install cost. Warm open is the median of ten runs per app; memory includes the whole process tree.

The 178.5 MiB memory reading caught a short GPU memory spike after the first frame, so use the current memory figures above instead.

Energy was not measured. Source-bearing bundles can also include SDK interfaces and assets; the historical analysis does not establish the current full-bundle install ratio.

Analysis: https://github.com/incyashraj/krate/blob/main/evidence/benchmarks/marktext-vs-krate/runs/20260825T085644Z/analysis.md
The public benchmark kit contains the protocol, analysis and seal. Retained raw run data is not all distributed in the public checkout.
